title: Four of eight DCU tasks that produced no qualified candidate at two turns qualified at four, and the eight larger-budget runs drew no provider fault at all

evidence.retained: bw1100 sweep-20260918-054910.tsv and its per-task logs: softsign, per_channel_moments, softmax, layernorm_gamma_beta_backward, gemm_silu, gemm_bias, channel_absmax_scale and attention_decode at four turns and a 400000 token budget, against the same eight tasks' earlier runs at two turns and 200000
sites: qualified at four turns having produced no qualified candidate at two: softsign, per_channel_moments, layernorm_gamma_beta_backward, attention_decode
unchanged at four turns: softmax, gemm_silu, gemm_bias, channel_absmax_scale
softsign's four-turn run reaches event 41; a two-turn run of the same task ends near 28
no run in the eight recorded protocol_adherence other than adhered

observation:
Half the failures were budget. Four tasks that had reached their token limit with nothing qualified reached a confirmed endpoint when given four turns instead of two, with no other change -- same model, same shapes, same commit. That includes attention_decode, which had faulted three times before, and layernorm_gamma_beta_backward and per_channel_moments, each of which had failed twice.

The mechanism is visible in the event counts rather than inferred: a refusal arrives after the author has written the thing, so recovering from one costs a turn, and a task whose first attempt draws a verifier refusal has one turn left at the two-turn budget. softsign's successful run reaches event 41 against roughly 28 for a two-turn run of the same task.

The four that did not convert fail for reasons more turns did not reach. softmax drew a different frontend refusal on each of three runs -- an unsupported `range`, then an undeclared name, then `broadcast takes one value and an explicit axis` together with an alias assignment -- which reads as the authoring surface rather than any one gap. gemm_silu and gemm_bias both evaluated candidates and qualified none, so those reached the device and lost on their measurement.

Worth recording and not worth explaining yet: none of the eight larger-budget runs drew a provider fault, and channel_absmax_scale is among them -- the task that had invoked Bash on four of four attempts at the smaller budget (F-2026-09-17-010). Eight runs is not enough to say the budget changed that, and the two differ in more than budget, since a longer run also spends more of its turns past the point where the task statement is fresh. It is a coincidence worth a second look, not a result.
proposed_change:
No Compiler or Lab change. What this establishes is about how a DCU sweep should be run rather than about the harness: two turns is below the point where a task can recover from its first verifier refusal, and a sweep at that budget measures the authoring surface's first-attempt hit rate rather than what the loop can reach.

If a sweep's purpose is coverage, four turns is the cheaper setting despite costing more per task, because a task that qualifies once is worth more than two that do not. If its purpose is to find authoring-surface defects, two turns surfaces them faster and this record is an argument for reading those sweeps as diagnostics rather than as results.

The provider-fault observation should be checked against a matched pair before anyone acts on it -- the same tasks at both budgets, counted -- rather than folded into F-2026-09-17-010 as though it were established.
